title: pvGenerateSurfaceNormals
body:
## pvGenerateSurfaceNormals

Deprecated ParaView alias of pvSurfaceNormals: the PolyDataNormals proxy was renamed SurfaceNormals, deprecated in ParaView 5.13 and is scheduled for removal in 5.14. It computes point normals on polygonal surfaces for smooth shading, with exactly the settings and behaviour of pvSurfaceNormals. Prefer pvSurfaceNormals in new documents.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Documents using this operation will need migration to pvSurfaceNormals when ParaView 5.14 is absorbed.
- Input must be polydata; extract a surface (surface) from volume meshes first.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `GenerateSurfaceNormals`. Identity: `filters/PolyDataNormals`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Normals Generation filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ComputeCellNormals` | This filter computes the normals at the points in the data set. In the process of doing this it computes polygon normals too. If you want these normals to be passed to the output of this filter, set the value of this property to 1. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Consistency` | The value of this property controls whether consistent polygon ordering is enforced. Generally the normals for a data set should either all point inward or all point outward. If the value of this property is 1, then this filter will reorder the points of cells that whose normal vectors are oriented the opposite direction from the rest of those in the data set. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `FeatureAngle` | The value of this property defines a feature edge. If the surface normal between two adjacent triangles is at least as large as this Feature Angle, a feature edge exists. If Splitting is on, points are duplicated along these feature edges. (See the Splitting property.) | `{"maximum":180.0,"minimum":0.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0` |
| `FlipNormals` | If the value of this property is 1, this filter will reverse the normal direction (and reorder the points accordingly) for all polygons in the data set; this changes front-facing polygons to back-facing ones, and vice versa. You might want to do this if your viewing position will be inside the data set instead of outside of it. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `NonManifoldTraversal` | Turn on/off traversal across non-manifold edges. Not traversing non-manifold edges will prevent problems where the consistency of polygonal ordering is corrupted due to topological loops. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PieceInvariant` | Turn this option to to produce the same results regardless of the number of processors used (i.e., avoid seams along processor boundaries). Turn this off if you do want to process ghost levels and do not mind seams. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `Splitting` | This property controls the splitting of sharp edges. If sharp edges are split (property value = 1), then points are duplicated along these edges, and separate normals are computed for both sets of points to give crisp (rendered) surface definition. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvGenerateSurfaceNormals",
  "inputs": {
    "Input": "UPSTREAM_Input"
  }
}
```
